_comment: SkyDive showcase targets. Positions are propagated by proper motion to epoch 2026.9 (astropy apply_space_motion from the 'ref' astrometry; parallax wobble ignored). Written with AI coding assistance (Claude Code).

targets.name: Barnard's Star
targets.blurb: The fastest-moving star in the sky: about 145" of travel across 14 years of WISE, 1.7 px across the SPHEREx visits, with hundreds of NEOSSat frames from the Canadian Space Agency.

targets.name: Epsilon Indi B
targets.blurb: A nearby brown dwarf pair, well detected by SPHEREx; it moves under 1 px across the SPHEREx visits and leaves a clear WISE track.
targets.note: Epsilon Indi A, 6.7' away, throws ghosts and glare that change between visits; no Pan-STARRS coverage this far south.

targets.name: WISE 0855−0714
targets.blurb: The coldest known brown dwarf: a 16-year track, detected at SNR 16 by stacking 4.1–4.75 µm, with a spectrum that rises to the red.
targets.note: Invisible in single frames; a faint star sits 7" away; the challenge coordinate is its old position, so it is moved by proper motion here and needs at least a 4' field.

targets.name: RW Aurigae
targets.blurb: A young variable star: labelled with its variability type and period, with per-visit brightness.

targets.name: R Draconis
targets.blurb: A Mira variable (period 246 days) in the SPHEREx deep field: monthly coverage, the best time sampling of any target.
targets.note: Saturated; a deep field with about 2,500 exposures, so about 600 spread evenly over every month and wavelength are loaded.
